messages.subject: Simsem: defining the known missing structure for simulated longitudinal data using miss(logit=script) function
parts:
Hi All,

I have tried to define the known missing structure for my Monte Carlo simulated longitudinal data. I have used miss(logit=script) function in which the missing structure is determined manually. Here is the code:

#missing data structure
script<-'maut1_1~p(0)
maut1_2~p(0.0)
maut1_3~p(0.0)
maut1_4~p(0.0)
maut2_1~p(0.112)
maut2_2~p(0.112)
maut2_3~p(0.112)
maut2_4~p(0.112)
maut3_1~p(0.174)
maut3_2~p(0.174)
maut3_3~p(0.174)
maut3_4~p(0.174)
paut1_1~p(0.073)
paut1_2~p(0.073)
paut1_3~p(0.073)
paut1_4~p(0.073)
paut2_1~p(0.452)
paut2_2~p(0.452)
paut2_3~p(0.452)
paut2_4~p(0.452)
paut3_1~p(0.346)
paut3_2~p(0.346)
paut3_3~p(0.346)
paut3_4~p(0.346)
REAPPRAISAL1~p(0.196)
SUPPRESSION1~p(0.196)
RUMINATION1~p(0.196)
SEX~p(0.0)
HOITO~p(0.0)
SES~p(0.0)'

missingness<-miss(logit=script, m=0)

AUTanalysis.POPCHILDHOOD.CHILDHOOD <-sim(nRep = 1000, model=AUTmodel.CHILDHOOD, n =546, generate= AUTmodelPOP.CHILDHOOD, lavaanfun = "sem", seed=565, std.lv=T, cilevel=0.90, miss=missingness, estimator="MLR")

The variables with the same proportions of missing values are measured at the same time point (e.g., REAPPRAISAL1, RUMINATION1, SUPPRESSION1). The simulation works just fine. However, I would like to define the missing structure by taking into account the longitudinal data structure. For example: if a participant has missing value in maut2_1, she/he would also have missing value in maut2_2, maut2_3, and maut2_4. 

Now the problem is that even though I manage to define the correct proportion of missingness for variables, the current script defines missingness randomly for each of these variables. By contrast, I would like to simulate the missing data structure in which a participant has missing values in all variables at time point x when she/he has missing values at this time point. So, I would like to somehow set these constraints/interdependencies in the script (e.g., that the maut2_1, maut2_2, maut2_3, and maut2_4 are missing from the same participant when there are missing values); yet, I have not found out how to do this.

So my questions are as follows:
1. Is it even possible to define these kinds of constraints in the missing value script?
2. If it is, any ideas about how to do that correctly?

Thank you for your help!

Best regards,

Jaakko Tammilehto

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Simsem: defining the known missing structure for simulated longitudinal data using miss(logit=script) function
parts:
Hi Jaakko,

I think you have two options to specify complete missingness at a time point. Instead of using the logit argument in the miss function you could use the prAttr argument to specify the proportion of data lost due to attrition at each time point. You can specify the same attrition rate at each time point or different attrition (e.g. increasing attrition across time). If you need a more specific approach to missingness, you can use the logical argument in the miss function. For this function you would create a logical matrix of TRUE and FALSE values with the same dimensions as your data and any cell with a value of TRUE will be missing in each simulation (note: this assumes MCAR missing, but based on your script that's what you're specifying so I think you're okay).

Hope this helps,

Alex

Hello again,

Ok, I have developed step by step using simsem. I have to repeat myself; It is an absolutely great R package and significant scientific contribution. Currently, I try to conduct a simulation study with some non-normal variables and missing data structure (longitudinal data). I formed a logical matrix for missing structure and added some skewness and kurtosis for some of the variables. My main interest is to assess statistical power to detect the correct model among different options based on model comparison. When I conducted the simulations, I got the following warning message for the following syntax: 

AUTanalysis.POPCHILDHOOD.CHILDHOOD <-sim(nRep = 1000, model=AUTmodel.CHILDHOOD, n =710, 
                                         generate= AUTmodelPOP.CHILDHOOD, lavaanfun = "sem", indDist = dist,  seed=565, std.lv=T, cilevel=0.90, miss=missingness, estimator="MLR")

Warning message:
In lavaan::parameterEstimates(out, standardized = TRUE, boot.ci.type = citype,  :
  lavaan WARNING: fmi only available if se = "standard"

I think the reason for this warning message is that I used "MLR" as an estimator method. When I checked the results of the simulation, all parameters seem logical (e.g., parameters with lowest N have the lowest power), convergence %=100, no negative variances, etc. As I said, my main focus is to assess statistical power to detect the correct model based on the scaled chi-square test. Moreover, in more descriptive purpose, I will report the model parameters. If I understand this warning correctly, it is only relevant if I would be interested in the fraction of missing values when estimating some descriptive statistics. In this case, I think it is not a problem? 


So, the question: Is my interpretation correct, or is this warning a problem to make valid inference about statistical power to detect the correct model based on model comparisons and checking and reporting model parameters?


-Jaakko
